heroHeadline: Federal Troops Reinforce Baidoa as Government Moves to Defuse Turkey Backlash Over Doolow Strike
heroSubtitle: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud ordered fresh Somali National Army reinforcements to Baidoa on September 9, 2026 to push back Laftagareen-aligned Darawish militia after the heaviest clashes yet in the city on September 3, though the retake operation had not begun as of September 9. Parliament Speaker Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jama sought to contain the fallout from the disputed September 3-4 Doolow drone strike on opposition-aligned Gen. Mahad Abdirahman 'Shub,' telling Somalis on September 10 that the wave of Turkish flag burnings across Jubaland, Puntland and Southwest State was a 'foreign agenda' rather than genuine sentiment, and urging the public not to let internal political disputes damage ties with Ankara — as the federal government continues to deny any external strike occurred. Separately, AFRICOM disclosed on September 11 a third airstrike within a week against Al-Shabaab near Quumbi, Jubbaland (50 miles northwest of Kismayo, conducted September 8), pushing the confirmed 2026 US airstrike total in Somalia past 81 and keeping the year on pace to approach 2025's record. The UN drawdown continues to accelerate: UNSOS remains in asset liquidation and staff layoffs as roughly 11,862 uniformed AUSSOM personnel depend on its logistics chain ahead of the US funding cutoff at year-end.
